title: Cut over code review to canonical policy discovery
description:
Atomically replace the repository-specific review prompt's duplicated engineering rubric with a procedure that loads applicable canonical prose, resolves relevant addressable policy, and emits auditable evidence and finding references. All prompt, wrapper, regression-test, and affected documentation changes land together so the code-review contract remains coherent when the cutover completes.

## Background

The canonical repository policy and backward-compatible structured-reference field are stable prerequisites. The repository-specific prompt owns review procedure, while the shared wrapper remains tool-agnostic and registry-owned statements remain in their configured sources of truth.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The review procedure treats every `AGENTS.md` from repository root to each affected path as the complete prose baseline, applies closer specialization, and reports unresolved contradictions.
- [hard] REQ-02: Qualified-item discovery is bounded to citations in applicable policy, issue content, relationship labels, linked documents, attributable patches, and directly implicated behavior; every collected item is resolved from its configured source of truth before it governs a judgment.
- [hard] REQ-03: The procedure treats `satisfies:`, `enforces:`, and `per:` labels as evidence claims, makes attributable dangling, contradictory, or unsupported claims blocking, and classifies unrelated pre-existing defects as advisory.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every review emits the five Markdown header fields `Attribution`, `Policy sources`, `Resolved items`, `Gate evidence`, and `Truncation recovery`, using `none` for every empty value.
- [hard] REQ-05: The procedure consumes the latest recorded required-gate evidence, leaves executable validation policy with `@/gate/jit-validate`, and does not rerun a currently passing gate.
- [hard] REQ-06: Findings governed by addressable policy carry valid resolved qualified IDs in `references`, findings based only on ordinary code correctness may use an empty array, and PID-signaling findings cite `@/inv/pid-safety` when that invariant governs them.
- [hard] REQ-07: `scripts/code-review-prompt.md` contains procedural discovery and judgment rules but no copied registry statements or replacement engineering rubric.
- [hard] REQ-08: `scripts/ai-review.sh` and `contrib/gates/ai-review.sh` remain behaviorally identical and tool-agnostic, document the optional references field in their common finding example, and pass a classified referenced finding through the existing verdict contract.
- [hard] REQ-09: Deterministic positive and negative tests cover policy precedence, bounded discovery, source-of-truth selection, relationship claims, evidence-header completeness and explicit empty values, structured references, legacy compatibility, wrapper parity, and rejection of duplicated registry prose.
- [hard] REQ-10: User-facing custom-gate documentation and contributor guidance explain policy ownership, applicable `AGENTS.md` discovery, addressable traceability, structured references, and the boundary between repository-specific prompts and tool-agnostic wrappers.
- [hard] REQ-11: All prompt behavior, policy regression tests, wrapper contract examples, and documentation required to validate the new review procedure are present together in the completed change.
